title: The Last Load to Storm Point
subtitle: A choose-your-route lighthouse cargo adventure

storm-depot.text:
Rain rattled on the roof of Storm Point depot. The lighthouse lamp had failed, and fog was coming.

Mia's six-wheel truck carried a new lamp, a heavy battery and repair tools. Tom climbed into the cab. Black Labrador Scout settled on his mat.

cargo-check.text:
The lamp sat inside a padded wooden crate. Four crossed straps held it to the truck bed. The battery box was lower and heavier.

Heavy cargo must be kept low. This helps a truck stay steady when the road tilts.

weather-board.text:
The board showed wind, rain and tide times. The harbour ferry could sail before the wind grew stronger. The old causeway would stay above water for one hour.

A forest road also crossed the hills, but fallen branches might block it.

lens-crate.text:
Tom checked the arrows painted on the crate. The lamp had to stay upright. Soft blocks protected its thick glass lens.

Mia could test the depot crane before leaving, or drive onto the weigh platform to check the load on each axle.

battery-crate.text:
The battery stored power for the lighthouse. Its box had a rubber seal to keep rain out. Beside it stood a case of cables and tools.

Scout sniffed the case. Tom spotted one loose catch before it could shake open.

ferry-port.text:
At the harbour, waves slapped the stone wall. A high-deck ferry waited behind the breakwater. The causeway road began farther along the bay.

The ferry was direct. The causeway was quicker, but only while the tide stayed low.

tide-chart.text:
Tom traced the curved tide line with one finger. The sea would soon cover the lowest stones.

Mia could use the causeway before the water rose, or turn inland to the longer forest road. Both routes reached Storm Point from different sides.

test-crane.text:
The crane lifted the lamp crate a hand's width. Its straps stayed tight and the crate remained level.

Mia lowered it gently. The crane test proved the harbour could unload it. A quarry crane offered another route if the ferry became too rough.

weigh-truck.text:
Numbers glowed on the weigh platform. The truck was heavy, but no axle carried too much. Mia checked the tyres as well.

The load was ready for either the wet forest road or the firm stone track through Grey Quarry.

seal-crate.text:
Tom pressed the waterproof seal into its groove. Mia closed every latch. Rain drummed on the box but could not reach the battery.

They could climb through the sheltered forest, or follow the open coast track where the ground was flatter.

pack-tools.text:
Tom sorted the tools into padded slots. Nothing could roll about when the truck leaned. Mia added spare cable and a bright work lamp.

The quarry road was rough but strong. The coast track was smoother but close to the rising sea.

high-ferry.text:
The truck rolled onto the ferry and stopped between steel guides. Thick chains held its wheels. Scout stayed safely in the cab with Tom.

Beyond the harbour wall, white waves crossed the bay. The captain could use the sheltered channel or aim straight for the island dock.

old-causeway.text:
Black and white posts marked the causeway. Wet stones shone between shallow pools. Mia stopped beside the tide gauge.

The centre road was still clear. A higher coast track curved around the bay, but it ended near a strip of soft beach.

forest-road.text:
The forest road climbed beneath bending trees. The truck's low gears helped it crawl without rushing. Scout's ears lifted at every crack of a branch.

Ahead, a fallen pine blocked one bend. A narrow side road continued towards the lighthouse gate.

quarry-road.text:
Grey Quarry rang with dripping water. The old stone road could carry great weight, but one slope was steep.

A parked quarry crane stood near a shorter track. The main road climbed safely around the long way to the lighthouse gate.

coast-track.text:
Wind pushed spray across the coast track. The lighthouse flashed weakly through the fog.

One route crossed firm beach sand below the cliffs. The other climbed a narrow shelf above the waves. Mia stopped to choose before the track divided.

storm-sea.text:
The ferry followed the sheltered channel. The cliffs blocked the strongest wind, but floating branches bumped against the bow.

The island dock was close. The captain could enter its narrow harbour, or lower the truck onto the broad landing beach nearby.

causeway-water.text:
Mia drove slowly between the posts. Water washed over one low patch, but it stayed below the wheel hubs. The engine's air intake remained high and dry.

Near the far end, a ramp led straight uphill. A side track joined the cliff shelf.

fallen-tree.text:
Mia fixed the winch rope around the fallen pine. Everyone stood well away from the tight line. The winch pulled slowly until the trunk slid clear.

A muddy shortcut led towards the lamp tower. The firm main road continued to the lighthouse gate.

stone-slope.text:
Loose stones rolled under the tyres. Mia selected the lowest gear before the climb. The truck moved at walking speed, with the lamp crate steady behind it.

At the top stood the quarry crane. A level track also ran to the lighthouse gate.

beach-sand.text:
Mia followed the darker, firmer sand. The truck kept moving gently so its tyres did not dig holes. Scout watched gulls lift from the shore.

A beach winch stood below the lighthouse. A rocky ramp joined the cliff shelf farther on.

cliff-shelf.text:
The shelf road was narrow, so Mia checked it on foot before driving. The outer edge was marked by strong stone posts.

The road reached the lighthouse gate. A second ramp dropped to the beach winch below the tower.

choices.text: Drop down to the beach winch

island-dock.text:
The ferry touched the dock without a bump. A dock crane could lift the lamp crate onto a small trailer. The truck could also leave the ferry and climb the old service road.

Above them, the lighthouse beam faded again.

lighthouse-gate.text:
Keeper Jo opened the iron gate. The truck had reached Storm Point, but the last yard was steep.

They could use the lighthouse's small lifting crane, or roll the battery trolley through the sheltered service tunnel beneath the tower.

emergency-choice.text:
The lamp crate hung level beneath the crane. The battery still had to reach the power room.

Tom could guide its trolley along the marked floor, or help Jo pull the padded lamp case into the lens room first.

crane-finish.text:
The crane placed the lamp beside the lens room. Tom guided the battery trolley over its yellow floor marks. Mia connected the thick cable, and Keeper Jo pressed the start button.

A bright beam swept across the bay. Scout barked once at the moving light.
crane-finish.ending: HARBOUR HERO — You delivered the last load by crane!

causeway-finish.text:
The service tunnel led straight beneath the lamp room. Its smooth floor made the heavy battery easy to roll. Soon the new lamp glowed above them.

Outside, the rising tide covered the old road, but Storm Point's beam shone safely over the water.
causeway-finish.ending: TIDE TRACKER — You beat the rising sea!

forest-finish.text:
Tom and Jo carried the padded lamp case into the lens room. Mia connected the battery below. The great glass lens turned, sending one bright flash across the wet forest and another over the sea.

Scout found a dry mat and fell asleep at once.
forest-finish.ending: FOREST GUIDE — You found the sheltered way!

quarry-finish.text:
The quarry crane lifted the lamp onto a small rail trolley. It rolled along an old level track to the lighthouse. The route looked forgotten, but it carried the load perfectly.

At dusk, the repaired lamp flashed over Grey Quarry and out across the bay.
quarry-finish.ending: STONE ROAD MASTER — You used the quarry route!

beach-finish.text:
The beach winch pulled the cargo trolley up its steel rails. Mia kept the truck on firm sand while Tom watched from the safe path.

The new lamp reached the tower before the fog. Its first beam made a silver road across the dark water.
beach-finish.ending: BEACH RESCUER — You hauled the light from the shore!
